UAE → Oman · Border rules · Last verified June 2026

Driving a Mortgaged Car from the UAE to Oman? You'll Need a Bank NOC

If your car is financed through a UAE bank and you're planning a road trip to Oman, you can't just drive across the border. Lenders, GCC border control, and customs all require a No Objection Certificate (NOC) from the bank that holds the lien on your vehicle. Travellers without one have been turned back at the border — including during peak Eid traffic.

Why an NOC is required

A car under a UAE bank loan is legally pledged to the lender until the loan is settled. Taking the vehicle out of UAE jurisdiction — even for a weekend in Muscat or Salalah — requires the bank's formal consent. Without it, customs officers at Omani entry points can refuse the vehicle.

What the NOC must contain

Your bank-issued NOC needs to:

  • Be on official bank letterhead and signed/stamped by an authorised officer
  • Include your vehicle chassis number, registration plate, and Mulkiya details
  • Include your Emirates ID number
  • State permission for the vehicle to enter Oman during a specified date range
  • Be notarised and translated into Arabic for the Omani side

What banks typically require from you

Most UAE banks require:

  • A refundable security deposit equal to the outstanding loan balance, plus a ~2% processing fee
  • A signed declaration of travel dates and destination
  • Processing time that can take up to two weeks in practice — banks publish 3–5 working day SLAs but notarisation and Arabic translation add real time on top

This is not something you can arrange at the border. Start the request at least two weeks before you plan to travel.

Borders where the NOC is checked

The requirement applies at all UAE–Oman land crossings:

Border postRouteTypical use
Hatta (Al Wajajah)Dubai → MuscatBusiest crossing
MezyadAl Ain → Buraimi / NizwaHeavy weekend traffic
Khatmat MilahahEast coast → SoharCoastal route
Al DarahNorthern MusandamKhasab trips

The good old days of just driving your financed car across the border are over. The rules have changed, and enforcement is now consistent across all crossings — particularly during Eid Al Fitr, Eid Al Adha, and UAE National Day weekends. Don't show up without the paperwork.

Other documents you'll need

The NOC is one piece. You'll also need:

  • Valid passport
  • Emirates ID
  • UAE driving licence (GCC residents do not need an International Driving Permit)
  • Vehicle registration card (Mulkiya)
  • Oman-valid car insurance — your standard UAE policy doesn't cover Oman. Either extend with your UAE insurer or buy an Orange Card at the border (around AED 100 for 7 days)

Bottom line

If your car is mortgaged: start the NOC paperwork at least two weeks before you travel, longer if you're going during a public holiday weekend. Budget for the refundable deposit. Without the NOC in hand, you risk a multi-hour return drive at best, and a cancelled trip at worst.
